correctness.rationale: Under the explicit partial-map composition convention and for every n>=0, a nonzero common mixed-product arrow forces an isolated, fully saturated 4-vertex diamond. Disjoint product arrows give disjoint diamonds, hence rank<=floor(n/4). Removing diamonds leaves exactly source-to-sink two-colored alternating paths and even cycles. Labeled path count 2*k! for k>=2 and even-cycle count 2*(2j-1)! for length 2j yield exp(z+2*z^2/(1-z))/(1-z^2). Every rank-r square-zero prescribed product uses 2r source/target vertices and (n-2r)!/(n-4r)! ordered intermediate assignments; leftover structures are exactly Z_{n-4r}. The formula for number of outputs n!/[r!(n-2r)!] yields the complete bivariate EGF. Independent all-pair enumeration for n<=7 checks every fiber; finite checks are corroboration only.

value.rationale: The product-rank distribution and exact multiplicity of each element as a product of two commuting square-zero partial bijections are canonical semigroup invariants. The sharp one-quarter rank ceiling reflects forced four-vertex diamond geometry, rather than a routine permutation of known involution counts. A full family of exact prescribed-product fibers and one two-variable enumerator captures all orders n and all possible ranks; such information is unavailable from aggregate commuting-pair totals or existing individual-element counts alone.
